abstract: This lecture by Dr. Ledbetter covers the fundamentals of musculoskeletal ultrasound of the knee, including tissue appearance (muscle, tendon, bone) and the critical concept of anisotropy. The speaker demonstrates a systematic scanning protocol starting suprapatellar to evaluate the quadriceps and patellar tendons, menisci, and collateral ligaments. Clinical applications focus on detecting knee effusions and performing ultrasound-guided joint injections, emphasizing that ultrasound improves accuracy and patient satisfaction compared to blind techniques.
key_points: Muscle appears feathery in long axis and starry in short axis; tendon shows parallel hyperechoic lines in long axis and dots in short axis.
Anisotropy means tissue brightness changes with probe angle; always keep the probe perpendicular to tendon and nerve to avoid false-positive tears.
Start knee ultrasound suprapatellar in long axis to identify quadriceps tendon, patella, fat pads, and femur; then rotate to transverse view.
Joint effusion is seen as an anechoic space above the suprapatellar fat pad; the space is nearly absent when no fluid is present.
Follow the patellar tendon from patella to tibia in long and short axis; avoid injecting through the tendon as it is painful.
The medial meniscus anterior horn appears as a triangle; ultrasound can rule in a tear but cannot rule one out.
The MCL is seen as hyperechoic parallel lines; dynamic varus/valgus stress can reveal gapping compared to the contralateral side.
Ultrasound is superior to physical exam for detecting knee effusion; a focused scan takes only seconds.
For ultrasound-guided knee injection, use a lateral suprapatellar approach; visualize the needle entering the joint space under the probe.
When anatomy is difficult to palpate, use ultrasound to mark an injection site off the patellar tendon medially or laterally.
Mark the injection site by crossing two lines drawn from the center of the ultrasound probe positions.
Use the opposite end of the Betadine stick to mark the skin to maintain sterility.
